':!docs/delivery'; grep -rn 'fetch(|request.raw|reply.raw|for await|pipe(|pipeline(|Readable|hijack' apps/api/src apps/worker/src; review of identity/routes.ts, identity/oidc.ts, access/policy.ts, access/records.ts, worker relay.ts/handlers.ts, db/cli.ts and migrate.ts
checks_run.expected: No weakening; no secrets; no CDN; no path that holds a connection or transaction while waiting on anything but the database
checks_run.actual: Upload: CSRF and authentication still run in preValidation before the handler. Phase 1 runs the same refusals in the same order (404/403/400 file name/428/409/422/not_a_file/body_required/raw stream only) and commits before the body is read; BE16's onSend Connection: close for incomplete bodies still applies. Phase 2 is store.receive, with the size limit and the raw-byte sha256 enforced while streaming, fsync, and no connection held. Phase 3 is openWrite (fresh ownership, transformation read, archived transformation), If-Match on the FOR UPDATE row, revision under the lock, a version-guarded update, the audit event, and finalise before COMMIT; the catch discards the final object and the .part. Download: no transaction while streaming. Worker: transactions run only SQL. Migrate: its own pg.Client, unaffected by the pool options. Pool: statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 30 s, connectionTimeoutMillis 10 s, and an error listener on every client (connect hook); isPoolCheckoutTimeout maps to 503. Incomplete-body mapping: the strict conjunction in hooks.ts:82-90 (complete === false, no syscall, Node's abort error or premature close of an aborted request), logged at info. FE9: setValues updaters are pure, and onValuesChange is reported from an effect. react-warning-guard.ts forwards every console.error unchanged and only records five React warning patterns; it mocks or silences nothing, and its own test covers the 'other console.error' case. No secrets and no CDN in the diff. Issues found, both PRE-EXISTING and raised as findings: (a) phase 3 re-authorises against the grants and session loaded at request start (identity/routes.ts:137), so an in-flight upload commits after a revocation or logout: F-DG2-440, Medium; (b) OIDC discovery runs inside an open transaction in GET /auth/login (identity/routes.ts:268, oidc.ts:37-59), which contradicts the 'no remote call' note in pool.ts:34: F-DG2-441, Low. Observation, not a finding (not reachable): the upload's catch (routes.ts:546-548) also wraps sendVersioned after COMMIT. A synchronous throw there would discard a committed object, but sendVersioned and toEvidence do not throw for a committed row, and Fastify handles serialization errors inside reply.send.

summary: DG2 round 12, candidate 5dfecce4 (source 8488e7a, 552 files; recomputed). F-DG2-411 and F-DG2-412 are CLOSED_VERIFIED. The round-11 probe re-run unchanged on Node 22 and 24: R8 /me answers in 10 ms (round 11: no answer), and R6a/R6d log no error. Its only failing assertion, R8b 'meMs > 1500', encoded the round-11 hold and is inverted by the fix. The adversarial round-12 probe confirms: no session idle in transaction and no row lock during stalled uploads; same-If-Match races give exactly [200, 409] with one revision and one object; an archive during the body gives 422; a COMMIT failure after finalise leaves nothing; an abort leaves no .part; genuine faults stay 500/503 at error level. All required checks ran and passed: typecheck, build, lint, OpenAPI lint (161 ops), no-CDN, format, unit 790/790 on Node 22 and 24 and under load, and integration 600/600 in both locale runs (migrations 0001-0019, the AUD sweep 146/146). Historical DG0 and DG1 validation pass. Two new PRE-EXISTING findings: F-DG2-440 (Medium, not mandatory): an in-flight upload commits after the uploader's grant is revoked or their session is logged out, because phase 3 re-authorises on the request-start grants and session (same result at round-11 23e6c0a2). F-DG2-441 (Low): OIDC discovery runs inside an open transaction in GET /auth/login, so an unresponsive IdP stalls signed-in users. Neither is Critical, High or mandatory, so under the assignment's rule the verdict is PASS; both should be repaired.
